Hi Talia — thanks for the context and the usage file. Quick summary below of a practical structure we’ve used for customers moving off monthly billing into an annual advance-pay:

1) Baseline: annual prepay paid upfront (Net 30) in a single invoice.
2) Discounting: tiered effective discount vs pay-as-you-go (PAYG): 10% at $250k ARR equivalent, 18% at $500k, 25% at $1M. For two-year commitments we layer an additional 4% / 6% across tiers (negotiable).
3) Ramp smoothing: staged consumption buckets (Month 1–3 at 40% of forecast, 4–6 at 70%, >6 at 100%). This protects both parties from sudden spikes and avoids large true-ups in month 1.
4) True-up / Overage: quarterly usage reporting with one annual true-up reconciled against the prepay. Overage billed at discounted PAYG rate or drawn from a capped overage allowance depending on the contract.
5) Early-payment credit: for upfront payment (within 14 days) we can apply a 2% credit on the invoice as an early-payment incentive.
6) Refund / termination: for enterprise customers we can add a prorated refund/credit schedule in the SOW for partial failures, with an operational SLA carve-out.

If you’d like, I can put numbers against your 6-month snapshot and show the delta vs your current monthly spend (two scenarios: 1yr prepay vs 2yr prepay). I’ve attached a term-sheet sketch (v1) and will run a quick model.

High level next steps:
- Confirm target ARR-equivalent for the commit (ballpark is fine).
- Decide whether NovaProd wants a single upfront invoice or annual invoice per year under a 2-year SOW.
- Legal to receive term-sheet and PO details after we align commercially.

Best,

Gavin — great questions; I'll address them and loop legal/finance internally to confirm final language. Quick answers and proposed mitigations:

1) Amortization statement: yes — we provide an invoice-level amortization schedule that flags monthly allocable expense for your accounting. We will include a template schedule with the invoice.

2) Year-2 usage protection: for 2-year commitments we typically include a step-down rebate (not a refund) if your consumption falls X% below agreed forecast. Example: if year-2 usage is <60% of forecast we provide a 25% rebate on the unused commitment up to a cap (this is reflected as a credit on the year-2 invoice). Alternatively, we can do a hybrid approach: 12-month opt-out after year 1 with a small termination fee (usually 10% of remaining commit).

3) Billing logistics: we accept PO + ACH/Bank transfer; invoice due net 30. For annual prepay we can issue one invoice per year or a single invoice for the full 2-year term depending on your procurement requirements.

Internal note to Aditya / Steph: we need to confirm the maximum rebate cap we can offer for NovaProd at each tier and whether legal is comfortable with the opt-out language. Aditya — can you run marginal economics (cost at our typical cluster configs) so we can propose a cap that preserves margin? Steph — please check with Legal on opt-out clause wording and standard termination fee amounts.

Thanks — Avery

Avery / Steph — ran the quick economics:

- Using the Horizon-40 pool assumptions and your projected 2.5x H1 growth, our marginal cost estimate for NovaProd is roughly $0.018 per 1k tokens at typical batch depths.
- If we offer a 25% discount at the $1M tier plus a 6% multi-year uplift for a 2-year commit, the blended effective price is ~ $0.0128 per 1k tokens — still within acceptable gross margins (~28% modeled).
- Rebate cap recommendation: for year-2 step-down rebate, cap at 25% of the committed invoice value. That keeps tail risk limited. If Legal prefers a soft opt-out (12-month), use a 10% termination fee of remaining commitment.

I also sketched a sample line-item structure we can offer:
- Year 1: $600k prepay (covers forecasted consumption at tier-level discount)
- Year 2 (2-yr SOW): $600k prepay with step-down rebate up to $150k if usage <60% of forecast; early-payment 2% credit if paid within 14 days; quarterly amortization schedule delivered with invoice.

If you want, I can forward this to Legal as a commercial recommendation.

Cheers,
Aditya
Principal, Revenue Operations

Subject: Final commercial proposal & next steps — NovaProd annual advance-pay (1yr vs 2yr)

Hi Talia / Gavin — thanks for the quick turn. Below is a concise statement of the commercial options we discussed. Once you confirm which lane (1yr single-pay or 2yr SOW + optional opt-out) you prefer, I’ll send a redlined term-sheet and an SOW + DocuSign package.

Option A — 1-year annual prepay (single invoice, paid upfront):
- Commit: $720,000 prepay covering forecasted 2027 consumption (baseline).
- Discount: effective 22% vs PAYG at this volume.
- Early-payment credit: 2% if remitted within 14 days.
- True-up: annual reconciliation, quarterly usage reporting; overage billed at discounted PAYG rate.
- Amortization: invoice-level monthly amortization schedule provided for finance.

Option B — 2-year commit (SOW with year-1 + year-2 invoices):
- Year 1: $600,000 prepay; Year 2: $600,000 prepay (same forecast).
- Multi-year uplift: additional 6% discount layered on year-level discounts above.
- Year-2 protection: step-down rebate up to 25% of year-2 invoice if usage <60% of forecast OR optional 12-month opt-out after year 1 with 10% termination fee on remainder.
- Early-payment credit: 2% each invoice if paid within 14 days.
- Billing: accepts PO + ACH; Net 30. Quarterly amortization schedule included.

Commercial asks from NovaProd: please confirm (a) preferred lane (A or B), (b) whether you want a single full-2yr invoice or per-year invoice under the 2yr SOW, and (c) any procurement constraints (PO numbers, required invoice fields).

Next steps once you confirm: legal will provision an SOW with chosen lane, accounting will prepare invoice template, and we’ll schedule a signing window of 7 business days to meet your internal procurement timeline.

Thanks again — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
